turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mr. Ellis, your wife made this appointment. What's been going on?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing of consequence, Doctor. I am quite well, and I cannot imagine this will take long.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He isn't, though. He asks me the same question four or five times in an afternoon.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has that been going on?
[SEG0005] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Um, a few months. Maybe since the spring — actually, I can't pin the start.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not repeat myself, Doctor. I merely confirm what was said.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Missed any appointments?
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The dentist. Twice. February, and then again in April. Both cards were still on the fridge.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I was not informed of the April visit. The February one — well, actually, I believe I attended.
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): You didn't, Harold. I sat in that waiting room by myself.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you gotten lost?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Certainly not.

[SEG0013] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Last Thursday he walked to the pharmacy on Maple. A neighbor — she brings us tomatoes every August, sweet lady — found him over by the old high school and drove him home.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I chose a longer route. I was not lost.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Were you confused?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose I paused a moment to get my bearings. That is hardly confusion.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Trouble finding words?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes. Not really.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any falls?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none at all.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Doctor.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Short of breath?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0027] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He is more tired, though. Most afternoons he nods off in the armchair.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Every afternoon?
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Most days, since around the same time as the questions. A few months.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I rest after lunch, as I always have. I would not call it fatigue.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sleeping through the night?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Adequately. I rise once to use the bathroom, and I am asleep again promptly.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It's two or three times, and he just lies there. He tells me he cannot settle.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I am simply being prudent about the bathroom. I sleep quite well.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Appetite?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Perfectly fine, thank you.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weight change?
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): His pants are loose. Maybe ten pounds since winter. He won't get on the scale for me.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I have been watching my portions. The change is intentional.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Who handles the medicines?
[SEG0041] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I do. Leave them with him and the evening ones sit in the cup.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I am perfectly capable of managing my own tablets, Doctor.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): What does he take?

[SEG0044] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Lisinopril, ten milligrams every morning, for his blood pressure. Atorvastatin, twenty milligrams at bedtime. And a baby aspirin, eighty-one milligrams, with breakfast.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything stopped recently?
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Hydrochlorothiazide. The kidney doctor — well, actually, his regular doctor — stopped it in January. The potassium came back low.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): The bottle remains in the cabinet. I have not taken a single tablet since.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does he take every dose?
[SEG0049] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Mornings, yes, I watch those. The statin, some nights he swears he already took it and it's still in the cup. Maybe three nights a week. I'm not really sure.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I take whatever is placed before me.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Home blood pressure?
[SEG0052] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Yesterday morning. One thirty-eight over eighty-four, on the arm cuff.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Misplacing things around the house?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): My reading glasses, on occasion. For perhaps two weeks. Nothing of importance.
[SEG0055] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Glasses, the keys, the remote. It's been since Christmas, so more like five months.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): I must disagree on the timing. Two weeks, not five months.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Still driving?
[SEG0058] person_3 (CAREGIVER): He took the car to the hardware store on Saturday. I didn't even know until he walked back in.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): The route is entirely familiar. I managed without the least difficulty.
[SEG0060] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any memory trouble or strokes in the family?
[SEG0061] person_3 (CAREGIVER): His mother got very forgetful in her eighties. Then she had a stroke.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): The stroke is correct. She was otherwise herself, in my opinion. I would not call it a disease.
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll get bloodwork, cholesterol, sugar, thyroid, B12, the usual. I don't think we need a memory clinic, and no scan. See you in six months if the labs are fine.
[SEG0064] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, he also left a burner on last week. I walked in and the whole kitchen smelled hot. With the getting lost, I'm frightened he'll go out again.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): The burner was low. I had stepped away for a moment only.

[SEG0066] person_1 (DOCTOR): All right, I'm changing the plan. Bloodwork still, this week, and I will refer you for a memory assessment. We might do a head scan if that assessment says we need one. Not now.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): I hardly think a memory clinic is warranted, but I will attend if you insist.
[SEG0068] person_1 (DOCTOR): Don't walk out alone for now. Your wife keeps the medicines. Bring the bottles to the assessment so the doses are straight.
[SEG0069] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can do that. I'll put them in my purse the night before.
[SEG0070] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back here in four weeks. We'll look at the blood results then. I'm not putting a name on this today.
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): Very well, Doctor. Thank you for your time.

spec.situation: Spouse brings an older person who 'is fine' but repeats questions, forgets appointments and got lost; patient disagrees on many points; medicines managed by spouse; doctor plans bloods and a memory assessment, no diagnosis said aloud.
features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

omissions.text: Possible trouble finding words: when asked, the patient said 'sometimes' though minimized it ('not really').

Weight loss detail is incomplete/uncertain: caregiver estimated his pants are loose and maybe about 10 pounds lost since winter, while the patient said the change was intentional from watching portions.
Hydrochlorothiazide discontinuation details missing: it was stopped in January by his regular doctor (caregiver first said kidney doctor, then corrected herself) because potassium was low.
Patient stated he has not taken any hydrochlorothiazide since it was stopped, despite the bottle remaining in the cabinet.
Medication adherence problem not captured for atorvastatin: caregiver reports the bedtime statin is still in the cup maybe three nights a week, while morning doses are watched and taken.
Home blood pressure context missing: the 138/84 reading was taken yesterday morning on an arm cuff.
Driving history is missing: he is still driving and drove to the hardware store on Saturday without his wife knowing.
Doctor initially said no memory clinic and no scan with follow-up in six months if labs were fine, but then changed the plan after the caregiver reported the burner incident and safety concerns.
Caregiver expressed safety concern that she is frightened he will go out again because of the burner being left on and the getting lost.
Follow-up plan detail missing: return in four weeks specifically to review the blood results; doctor said he is not putting a name on this today.
